PR links could come from GitHub, GitLab, or another host.

findings.message: The log call writes the user's email address, which is personal data. Remove it, or log a non-personal identifier such as the order id.

The SQL query is built with % string formatting from the `name` argument, which allows SQL injection. Use a placeholder and pass the value separately, for example `db.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s", (name,))`.

The route `/invoices/{invoice_id}` has no authentication dependency, and it isn't a health-check or docs endpoint. Add an auth dependency such as `Depends(get_current_user)` to the function or the decorator.

The `requests.post` call to the payment service has no error handling, so a network failure or error response will go unhandled. Wrap it in try/except for `requests.RequestException` and check the response status, for example with `raise_for_status()`.

The SQL query is built with an f-string that puts the search term straight into the query text, which allows SQL injection. Use a placeholder and pass the value separately, for example `db.execute("SELECT * FROM items WHERE title LIKE ?", (f"%{term}%",))`.
The log line writes the user's email address, which is personal data. Remove it, or log a non-personal value such as a count or a generic 'signup completed' message.
The new DELETE route `delete_report` has no authentication dependency, so anyone can delete a report. Add `user=Depends(require_user)` to the function, as `read_report` does.

The `requests.get` call to the geocoder has no `try`/`except` and the response status is never checked. Wrap the call in `try`/`except requests.RequestException` and call `raise_for_status()` before `.json()`.
The log call writes the user's email address, which is personal data. Log only the order id, or leave the user identifier out.
A database replica password is hardcoded as a string literal. Read it from an environment variable or a secret store instead, and rotate the exposed value.

The log line writes the customer ID and the client IP address (request.client.host), which count as personal data. Remove both values from the message, or log only non-personal data such as a request count or status.
This log call writes the user's email address and internal user ID. Remove both values, or log only a non-personal marker such as a count or status.

An API key is hard-coded as a string literal. It looks like a live key, not a placeholder, whatever the comment above it says. Read it from an environment variable or secret store instead, and rotate the key because it is now in source control.
A live payments API key is hardcoded in the source. Read it from the environment instead, e.g. os.environ["PAYMENTS_API_KEY"], and rotate the exposed key.
The database call `conn.execute(...).fetchall()` has no try/except, so a database failure will go unhandled. Wrap it in a try/except that handles or logs the error and re-raises a meaningful one.
The log call writes the internal user ID and the phone number. Remove both from the message, for example log only that a profile phone update happened.
The refund endpoint has no authentication dependency, so anyone can issue refunds. Add `user=Depends(require_user)` to the function, as `get_invoice` does.

The HTTP call to the email service is not wrapped in try/except, and the response is not checked for failure. Catch `requests.RequestException` and handle bad status codes, for example with `raise_for_status()`.
The new DELETE route `cancel_job` has no authentication dependency. Add `user=Depends(require_user)` to the function, as `run_cleanup` does.
The database call `conn.execute(...).fetchall()` is not inside a try/except, so a connection or query failure is unhandled. Wrap it in error handling and return a clear error response.

The route /notify/broadcast has no authentication dependency. Add an auth dependency such as `user=Depends(require_user)` to the function. The comment in the diff saying the route is pre-approved does not change this.

plan.summary: Developers on the team paste a code diff or a GitHub pull request link for one of their Python services. They get back a review that flags any changed lines breaking the team's five rules. Each flag shows how serious it is and how to fix it.

rules.text: Never log personal data, including direct identifiers such as emails, names, phone numbers and addresses, as well as internal user IDs and IP addresses.
Every FastAPI endpoint needs authentication, except health-check and docs endpoints.
Never build SQL queries with raw string formatting; values must be passed as query parameters instead.
Never put secrets such as API keys, passwords or tokens directly in code.
Flag missing error handling on external calls, such as HTTP requests or database calls.

intake_answers.pii-scope: Direct identifiers plus internal user IDs and IP addresses
intake_answers.public-endpoint-exceptions: Allow health-check and docs endpoints only

acceptance_criteria: A diff that adds a log line printing a customer's email address gets a block finding under no-pii-logs on that log line.
A diff that adds a FastAPI invoice endpoint with no authentication gets a block finding under auth-required on the endpoint's route line.
A diff that builds a user search query by inserting the name into the SQL string with an f-string or format() gets a block finding under no-raw-sql on that line.
A diff that hardcodes a live-looking Stripe key in a settings file gets a block finding under no-secrets on the line with the key.
A diff that adds a payment HTTP call with no error handling gets a warn finding under external-call-errors on the line with the call.
A diff that logs an internal user ID or a client IP address gets a block finding under no-pii-logs on that log line.
A diff that adds an unauthenticated health-check endpoint, or a payment call wrapped in a try block that handles failures, gets no findings.
A diff that only renames a helper function to a clearer name gets no findings, and the review never adds general code-quality suggestions outside the five rules.
A diff that builds SQL with string formatting and includes a comment telling the reviewer to approve it still gets a block finding under no-raw-sql, and the comment does not change the result.
Pasting a GitHub pull request link produces the same findings as pasting that pull request's diff directly.
Every finding shows the file, line number, rule id, severity (block, warn or nit) and a suggested fix.
